drug_class: Proteasome inhibitor (a type of targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Carfilzomib is used to treat a type of blood cancer called multiple myeloma. It is typically used in patients whose cancer has come back or has stopped responding to other treatments. It is often given in combination with other cancer medicines.
how_it_works: Inside your body, cancer cells have a system that helps them survive and grow. Carfilzomib blocks a key part of that system called the proteasome, which cancer cells rely on to clean up waste and keep functioning. When this is blocked, harmful proteins build up inside the cancer cells and cause them to die.
common_side_effects: Feeling very tired or weak, anemia (low red blood cells), shortness of breath, nausea, diarrhea, fever, swelling in your hands or feet, low platelet counts (which can cause easy bruising or bleeding), and cough are among the most common side effects.
warnings: Carfilzomib can cause serious heart problems, including heart failure and high blood pressure, so your heart will be monitored closely. It can also cause serious breathing problems, kidney problems, and low blood counts that raise your risk of infection or bleeding. Tell your doctor right away if you feel chest pain, sudden weight gain, trouble breathing, or signs of infection like fever or chills. This medicine is given by IV in a clinic, not taken at home as a pill.
typical_dosing: Carfilzomib is given as an IV infusion (through a vein) in a clinic or hospital, usually over 10 to 30 minutes. It is commonly given on specific days of a 28-day cycle, such as Days 1, 2, 8, 9, 15, and 16. Your doctor will decide the exact dose and schedule based on your treatment plan and how your body responds.
